name: OpenMausBot
cost: Free (Apache 2.0). Bots run on the agent logins you already have. Boat cloud computers are paid after a trial
works_with: The claude, codex and grok CLIs, on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu 24.04
short: A chat app where every contact is a real AI agent with its own model, its own computer and its own connected apps.
what: OpenMausBot works like a messaging app for agents. Each bot in the sidebar runs the claude, codex or grok CLI on your machine and has its own personality and model. A bot can work on a cloud Linux desktop, a local VM or, where supported, your own computer, and can use hundreds of apps through Composio. Shell commands, file edits and questions appear in the chat as cards you allow or deny.
who: People who already use Claude Code, Codex or Grok and want several agents they can talk to like contacts. You need at least one of those CLIs installed and logged in, so skip it if you have none.
needs: macOS (Apple silicon or Intel), Windows x64 or Ubuntu 24.04 x64
At least one agent CLI installed and logged in: `claude`, `codex` or `grok`
Optional: a Composio project key for connected apps, a Boat API key for cloud computers, and an ElevenLabs or Fish Audio key for voices
For the terminal version or a source build: Node 24 or newer (and pnpm for the source build)

steps.title: Download the app
steps.text: Get the .dmg, the Windows installer or the Ubuntu .deb from the latest GitHub release. The harness server comes built in. The Windows installer isn't code-signed yet, so SmartScreen shows "unknown publisher". Choose More info, then Run anyway.

steps.title: Or run it from a terminal
steps.text: `npx openmausbot` also works without a global install. The first launch asks how you want to reach AI, which model to use and whether to connect a phone.

steps.title: Or build it from source
steps.text: Keep the server and app running, then start the desktop shell.
steps.code:
git clone https://github.com/milind-soni/OpenMausBot && cd OpenMausBot
pnpm install
pnpm dev:server    # harness server → 127.0.0.1:8799
pnpm dev           # app → http://127.0.0.1:5199
pnpm dev:desktop   # Electron shell; keep the two commands above running

steps.title: Add keys only if you want them
steps.text: Local chat works with none. Paste a key once in App Settings (the gear in the sidebar footer) to turn on connected apps, cloud computers or voices.

steps.title: Approve what bots do
steps.text: Shell commands, file edits and questions show up as inline cards. Pick Allow or Deny, or answer in the chat.

try.label: From the README
try.text: "Every weekday at 9, send me a summary of my inbox." The bot sets up the schedule in that turn and shows a card with Edit, Pause and Undo. Connect Gmail first.

watch: Bots run agent CLIs on your machine. On macOS and Ubuntu Xorg they can also control your own computer once you opt in. That is turned off on Ubuntu Wayland.
When a bot creates a schedule or webhook trigger, it does so without asking. You get a card to edit, pause or undo it.
Boat is a paid service after its trial, and cloud computers may cost money. Composio and Boat have their own accounts and terms.
The terminal version saves API keys as plain text in a private `config.json`.
Usage analytics are anonymous and optional. Turn them off in Settings, General, Usage analytics.
Ubuntu builds are beta, and voice calls are macOS only for now.
The project has no crypto token. The maintainer says any coin using its name has nothing to do with it.
